examples.en: The soldiers shot down an enemy plane.

examples.ko: 방어 시스템이 날아오는 드론을 격추할 거예요.
examples.en: The defense system will shoot down the incoming drone.
I saw a news report about the incident in which a fighter jet was shot down.

examples.ko: 게임에서 적 비행기를 다 격추하고 점수를 얻었어요.
examples.en: In the game, I shot down all the enemy planes and earned points.

examples.ko: 적을 격추해야 다음 단계로 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to shoot down the enemy to move on to the next level.
A scene of a plane being shot down appears in the movie.

explain: '쏘다'는 총이나 미사일을 쏘는 행동이고, '격추하다'는 날아다니는 비행기나 드론을 쏴서 떨어뜨리는 결과까지 나타내요. 목적어는 비행기, 드론처럼 하늘에 떠 있는 것만 와요. 뉴스와 게임에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: '쏘다' (to shoot) is the act of firing, while '격추하다' also includes the result: the target is brought down. The object is always something in the air, such as a plane or a drone. You hear it often in the news and in games.

en: wooden structure; made of wood (homonym: woodcarving)

examples.en: Because this house is made of wood, it is cool in summer.

examples.ko: 오래된 목조 건물이 아직도 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Old wooden buildings still remain.
A wooden bridge is slippery when it rains.
Most temples were built of wood.

examples.ko: 불이 나면 목조 주택이 더 위험해요.
examples.en: In a fire, wooden houses are more dangerous.

examples.ko: 목조 한옥에서 하룻밤 자 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to spend a night in a wooden hanok.

explain: 집, 건물, 다리처럼 큰 구조물에 주로 써요. 보통 '목조 건물', '목조 주택'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여요. 짝이 되는 말은 돌로 지은 '석조'예요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for large structures such as houses, buildings and bridges, usually before a noun: '목조 건물', '목조 주택'. Its counterpart is '석조', meaning built of stone.

examples.ko: 이 마을에서 유명한 문인이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many famous literary figures came from this town.

examples.ko: 문인들이 모여 시를 읽는 행사가 열려요.
examples.en: An event is held where writers gather and read poems.

examples.ko: 그분은 시와 소설을 모두 쓰는 문인이에요.
examples.en: That person is a writer who writes both poems and novels.
I toured the house of a literary figure from the Joseon period.
I was invited to a gathering of writers for the first time.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 옛날 문인들이 자주 오던 곳이에요.
examples.en: This cafe is a place that literary figures of the past often visited.

explain: '작가'는 지금 글을 쓰는 사람을 넓게 가리켜요. '문인'은 시, 소설, 수필을 쓰는 사람을 조금 격식 있게, 또는 옛날 느낌으로 부를 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '작가', '시인', '소설가'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: '작가' broadly refers to anyone who writes today. '문인' is a slightly formal, old-fashioned way to call someone who writes poems, novels or essays. In everyday talk, '작가', '시인' and '소설가' are more common.

examples.ko: 우리 시는 방재 계획을 새로 세웠어요.
examples.en: Our city made a new disaster prevention plan.

examples.ko: 태풍이 오기 전에 방재 훈련을 했어요.
examples.en: We held a disaster prevention drill before the typhoon came.

examples.ko: 방재 시설이 잘 되어 있어서 피해가 적었어요.
examples.en: The disaster prevention facilities were well built, so the damage was small.

examples.ko: 방재 담당자가 주민들에게 안내 문자를 보냈어요.
examples.en: The disaster prevention officer sent a text message to the residents.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오는 지역은 방재가 특히 중요해요.
examples.en: Disaster prevention is especially important in areas with heavy rain.
I received disaster prevention training at school.

explain: 뉴스나 공문서에서 자주 보는 말이고, 보통 '방재 훈련', '방재 시설'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '재난 대비'라고 더 쉽게 말해요. 발음이 같은 '방제'(병해충을 막는 일)와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: You often see it in the news and official notices, usually before a noun: '방재 훈련', '방재 시설'. In everyday talk people say '재난 대비' instead. Do not confuse it with '방제', which means controlling pests and plant diseases.

examples.en: The offender came out after finishing a five-year prison term.

examples.ko: 복역 중인 사람도 편지를 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: People who are serving time can also write letters.
The term was long, so the family had a hard time.

examples.ko: 복역 후에 새 일을 찾는 사람들을 돕는 단체예요.
examples.en: It is an organization that helps people find new jobs after serving their sentence.

examples.ko: 복역이 끝나기 전에 가석방될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Release on parole is possible even before the term ends.

examples.ko: 영화는 오랜 복역 끝에 자유를 얻은 사람의 이야기예요.
examples.en: The film tells the story of a person who gained freedom after a long prison term.

explain: '복역'은 징역 같은 형을 받고 교도소에서 지내는 기간 자체를 가리켜서, 보통 '복역 중', '복역 기간'으로 써요. 동사는 '복역하다'예요. 같은 상황에서 '감옥살이'는 더 구어체예요.
explain_en: '복역' refers to the time spent in prison under a sentence, and is usually used as '복역 중' or '복역 기간'. The verb form is '복역하다'. '감옥살이' describes the same situation in a more colloquial way.

examples.en: That person served a three-year sentence.

examples.ko: 그 사건의 범인은 지금 복역하고 있어요.
examples.en: The culprit in that case is serving time now.

examples.ko: 형기를 다 복역하면 나올 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once the full sentence is served, release is possible.

examples.ko: 오래 복역한 사람을 인터뷰한 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book of interviews with a person who served a long sentence.
The state decides where a sentence is served.
Some people do not change even after serving five years.

explain: 형을 받는 일은 '선고받다', 그 형을 실제로 사는 일은 '복역하다'예요. '징역을 살다'가 같은 상황에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요. 보통 '3년 복역했어요'처럼 기간과 함께 써요.
explain_en: Receiving the sentence is '선고받다', while actually living it out is '복역하다'. '징역을 살다' is an easier way to say the same thing. It is usually used with a length of time, as in '3년 복역했어요'.

examples.en: In the old days, news was sent far away by signal fires.
I saw a scene of lighting a signal fire on a mountaintop.
Beacon towers were built in high places.
When the signal fire went up, soldiers gathered.
I learned about the signal fire system at the museum.
This mountain is famous as a signal fire site.

explain: '횃불'은 손에 들거나 세워 두는 불이고, 봉화는 높은 산에서 연기와 불로 멀리 신호를 보내던 옛날 방식이에요. '봉화를 올리다', '봉화를 피우다'로 써요. 지금은 역사 이야기나 사극에서 주로 들어요.
explain_en: '횃불' is a torch you hold or set up, while '봉화' was an old way of sending signals over long distances with smoke and fire from high mountains. It is used as '봉화를 올리다' or '봉화를 피우다'. Today you mostly hear it in history stories and historical dramas.

examples.en: The hospital gave the patient a blood transfusion.

examples.ko: 사고로 피를 많이 흘려서 바로 수혈해야 해요.
examples.en: A lot of blood was lost in the accident, so a transfusion must be given right away.
Before giving a transfusion, they check the blood type.
The doctor is getting ready to give a transfusion.
I heard they gave a transfusion during yesterday's surgery.
After a blood transfusion, the body gets much better.

explain: '수혈하다'는 '환자에게 수혈하다'처럼 피를 넣어 주는 쪽에서 써요. 받는 사람 입장에서는 '수혈을 받다'라고 해요. 피를 내주는 일은 '헌혈하다'예요.
explain_en: '수혈하다' is used from the side giving blood to the patient, as in '환자에게 수혈하다'. From the patient's side, you say '수혈을 받다'. Donating blood is '헌혈하다'.

examples.en: That child was called a piano prodigy.
It was in the news that a prodigy had appeared.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 수학 신동이라는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I have been called a math prodigy.

examples.ko: 일곱 살에 대학 수업을 들은 신동을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met a prodigy who took college classes at the age of seven.
Prodigies often become ordinary as they grow up.
This movie is about a Go prodigy.

explain: '천재'는 나이와 상관없이 뛰어난 사람이고, '신동'은 어린아이일 때 이미 어른 같은 재능을 보이는 아이예요. 보통 '피아노 신동', '수학 신동'처럼 분야 이름을 앞에 붙여요. 어른에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '천재' is an outstanding person at any age, while '신동' is a child who already shows adult-level talent. A field is usually put in front: '피아노 신동', '수학 신동'. It is not used for adults.

examples.en: This chair is really comfortable when you sit in it.
I want to rest well in a cozy home.
The hotel room was more comfortable than I expected.
Grandmother is enjoying a comfortable retirement.

examples.ko: 안락하다고 해서 꼭 행복한 것은 아니에요.
examples.en: Being comfortable does not always mean being happy.
If the plane seat is comfortable, a long flight is fine too.

explain: '편안하다'는 몸과 마음이 편한 느낌 전체에 쓰고, '안락하다'는 집, 의자, 생활처럼 환경이 편하고 걱정 없이 지낼 만하다는 쪽이에요. 조금 격식 있는 말이라 일상에서는 '편해요'를 더 많이 써요. '안락한 생활', '안락한 의자'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '편안하다' covers any feeling of ease in body and mind, while '안락하다' is about a setting such as a home, a chair or a lifestyle that is comfortable and free of worry. It sounds a little formal, so '편해요' is more common in daily talk. Typical uses are '안락한 생활' and '안락한 의자'.

examples.en: The two companies agreed on the price by contract.
If you commit to a two-year contract on the phone, they give a discount.

examples.ko: 은행과 약정한 대로 매달 돈을 넣고 있어요.
examples.en: I put money in every month as agreed with the bank.
We first sort out what to stipulate in the contract.
The interest rate was not agreed on separately.

examples.ko: 약정해 놓고 안 지키면 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: If you agree and then do not keep it, it becomes a problem.

explain: '약속하다'는 일상에서 사람끼리 하는 약속이고, '약정하다'는 계약서, 은행, 통신사처럼 조건을 문서로 정해 둘 때 써요. 휴대폰 '약정'은 몇 년 동안 쓰기로 한 계약을 가리켜요. 명사 '약정'과 함께 '약정을 맺다'로도 써요.
explain_en: '약속하다' is an everyday promise between people, while '약정하다' is for fixing conditions in writing, as with contracts, banks and phone companies. A phone '약정' is a contract to keep using it for some years. The noun '약정' also appears as '약정을 맺다'.

examples.en: Grandfather's memorial portrait was placed at the funeral hall.
I bowed in front of the memorial portrait.
The family laid flowers before the memorial portrait.

examples.ko: 영정 사진을 미리 찍어 두는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people have their memorial photo taken in advance.

examples.ko: 영정 속 웃는 얼굴을 보니 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: Seeing the smiling face in the memorial portrait brought tears.
I carried my father's memorial portrait to the burial site.

explain: 장례식에서만 쓰는 말이라 평소 사진에는 쓰지 않아요. '영정 사진', '영정을 모시다'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '고인의 사진'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used only for funerals, never for ordinary photos. Typical uses are '영정 사진' and '영정을 모시다'. In daily talk, people sometimes just say '고인의 사진' (the photo of the deceased).

examples.en: Hot lava flows out of the volcano.
Lava becomes hard rock when it cools.
Jeju Island has caves formed from lava.
There is a tour where you can see lava up close.
The whole village disappeared because of the lava.
In the movie, the main character crosses over lava.

explain: 화산에서 나온 뒤의 뜨거운 액체 상태의 돌은 '용암', 땅속에 있을 때는 '마그마'라고 해요. 식어서 굳으면 '화산암'이 돼요. '용암이 흐르다', '용암이 분출하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Once out of the volcano, the hot liquid rock is '용암' (lava); while still underground it is '마그마' (magma). When it cools and hardens it becomes '화산암'. Common uses are '용암이 흐르다' and '용암이 분출하다'.

examples.en: In an emergency, call 119 right away.
The patient was in critical condition, so the surgery was rushed.

examples.ko: 위급 상황을 알리는 사이렌이 크게 울렸어요.
examples.en: A siren announcing the emergency rang out loudly.

examples.ko: 아버지가 위급하다는 연락을 받고 급히 갔어요.
examples.en: I got word that my father was in critical condition and hurried over.
In the emergency room, critical patients are treated first.

examples.ko: 위급할 때 침착하게 행동하는 것이 중요해요.
examples.en: It is important to act calmly in a crisis.

explain: '위급'은 '위급하다'로 더 많이 써요. '위급한 상황', '위급할 때'처럼 목숨이나 안전이 위험하다는 쪽이에요. '응급'은 급히 처치해야 하는 상황에 쓰고 '응급실', '응급 처치'에 붙어요.
explain_en: The noun is used less often than the adjective '위급하다', as in '위급한 상황' and '위급할 때'; it points to danger to life or safety. '응급' is for situations needing immediate treatment and appears in '응급실' and '응급 처치'.

examples.en: This action goes against the company rules.

examples.ko: 법에 위배되는 일은 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not do anything that violates the law.
The decision went against the promise, so I protested.

examples.ko: 계약 내용에 위배될 경우 벌금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: If it goes against the contract terms, a fine must be paid.
A ruling came out saying it violates the constitution.

examples.ko: 학교 규정에 위배되지 않는 선에서 해 보세요.
examples.en: Try it within limits that do not go against school regulations.

explain: '어기다'는 사람이 규칙을 직접 어기는 행동이고, '위배되다'는 행동, 결정, 내용이 법, 규칙, 약속에 맞지 않을 때 써요. 그래서 주어는 사람보다 일이나 결정이고, 조사 '에'와 함께 '규칙에 위배되다'로 써요. 계약과 법 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '어기다' is when a person breaks a rule directly. '위배되다' is used when an action, decision or content does not match a law, rule or promise, so the subject is usually a matter or decision rather than a person. It takes '에', as in '규칙에 위배되다', and appears often in contract and legal talk.

examples.ko: 유명세 때문에 마음대로 외출을 못 해요.
examples.en: Because of the price of fame, going out freely is hard.
Stars are bound to pay the price of fame.
As the fame grew, privacy shrank.
With more popularity comes the price of fame.

examples.ko: 어디를 가도 사진을 찍히는 것도 유명세예요.
examples.en: Being photographed wherever you go is also part of the price of fame.

examples.ko: 유명세에 지쳐서 가수가 잠깐 쉬기로 했어요.
examples.en: Worn out by the burdens of fame, the singer decided to take a short break.

explain: '인기'는 사람들이 좋아하는 것이고, '유명세'는 유명해진 대가로 겪는 불편이에요. 그래서 '유명세를 치르다'처럼 '치르다'와 함께 써요. 사생활 침해나 악플 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '인기' is being liked by many people, while '유명세' is the inconvenience you suffer as the cost of being famous. That is why it goes with '치르다' (to pay): '유명세를 치르다'. It often comes up in talk about privacy invasion and malicious comments.

examples.en: The raising of the sunken ship has begun.
The salvage work took a month.
The salvage was postponed because of bad weather.
The salvage succeeded, and the families shed tears.
The raising of the ship and the investigation proceed separately.

examples.ko: 오랜 인양 끝에 유물이 바다 위로 올라왔어요.
examples.en: After a long salvage, the relics came up from the sea.

explain: '인양'은 물에 가라앉은 배, 차, 유물을 끌어올리는 일에 써요. 사람이나 작은 물건을 건질 때는 '건지다', '구조하다'를 써요. 뉴스에서 '선박 인양', '인양 작업'으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '인양' is for raising sunken ships, cars or relics out of the water. For rescuing people or fishing out small things, use '건지다' or '구조하다'. In the news you often see '선박 인양' and '인양 작업'.

examples.en: They raised the car that had fallen into the sea.
They plan to raise the ship with a crane.

examples.ko: 침몰한 배를 인양하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Raising the sunken ship took a month.
Before raising the relics, they check their condition.
They decided to raise the ship and investigate the cause.
Relics that were raised are kept in a museum.

explain: '끌어올리다'는 위로 올리는 일 전체에 쓰고, '인양하다'는 물속에 가라앉은 큰 물건을 끌어올릴 때만 써요. 목적어는 '배', '차', '유물' 같은 것이에요. 일이 이루어진 쪽에서는 '인양되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '끌어올리다' covers pulling anything upward, but '인양하다' is used only for raising large things that sank in water. The object is something like a ship, a car or relics. When the thing is the subject, it becomes '인양되다'.

examples.ko: 그 나라의 지배자는 강한 군대를 가지고 있었어요.
examples.en: The ruler of that country had a strong army.
The new ruler changed the laws.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 여러 지배자에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned about several rulers.

examples.ko: 이 게임에서는 마지막에 이긴 사람이 섬의 지배자가 돼요.
examples.en: In this game, the last person to win becomes the ruler of the island.
Everyone had to follow the words of the ruler.

examples.ko: 시장을 지배자처럼 휘두르는 큰 회사가 있어요.
examples.en: There are big companies that wield the market like a ruler.

explain: '왕'은 나라를 다스리는 직위 이름이고, '지배자'는 직위와 상관없이 힘으로 사람이나 땅을 다스리는 사람이에요. 그래서 '시장의 지배자'처럼 비유로도 쓰고, 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 반대는 '피지배자'예요.
explain_en: '왕' is a title for the one who governs a country, while '지배자' is anyone who controls people or land by power, whatever the title. So it is also used figuratively, as in '시장의 지배자', and carries a slightly negative feel. The opposite is '피지배자'.

examples.ko: 차명 계좌를 쓰면 법에 걸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Using an account under a borrowed name can get you into legal trouble.

examples.ko: 사장은 가족 이름을 빌려 차명으로 주식을 샀어요.
examples.en: The boss bought stocks under a borrowed name, using a family member's name.
The use of borrowed names came to light, and an investigation followed.

examples.ko: 차명에 의한 거래는 금지된 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Transactions made under a borrowed name are banned in many cases.
It is hard to find assets held under borrowed names.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 차명 거래 때문에 문제가 커졌다고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said the problem grew because of dealings under borrowed names.

explain: 남의 이름을 빌려 쓰는 일이라서, 보통 '차명 계좌', '차명 재산', '차명 거래'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요. 자기 이름으로 하는 것은 '실명'이라고 해요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 자주 나오고 대체로 좋지 않은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It means using someone else's name, and is usually put before a noun: '차명 계좌', '차명 재산', '차명 거래'. Doing it under your own name is '실명'. It shows up often in news and legal talk and usually has a negative feel.

examples.ko: 삼촌이 사고로 척수를 다쳐서 휠체어를 타요.
examples.en: My uncle injured his spinal cord in an accident and uses a wheelchair.
The spinal cord is inside the spine.
The doctor suggested a spinal cord test.

examples.ko: 척수가 손상되면 감각이 사라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the spinal cord is damaged, feeling can be lost.

examples.ko: 척수에 문제가 생기면 몸을 움직이기 어려워요.
examples.en: If there is a problem with the spinal cord, it is hard to move the body.

examples.ko: 척수의 신경을 다시 살리는 연구가 진행 중이에요.
examples.en: Research on reviving the nerves of the spinal cord is under way.

explain: '척추'는 등뼈이고 '척수'는 그 안을 지나는 신경 다발이에요. 이름이 비슷해도 뼈와 신경으로 달라요. 의료 이야기에서 '척수 손상', '척수 신경'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '척추' is the backbone, and '척수' is the bundle of nerves running through it. The names are similar, but one is bone and the other is nerve. In medical talk you see '척수 손상' and '척수 신경'.

examples.en: A break from old ways is needed.

examples.ko: 뱀은 자라면서 탈피를 여러 번 해요.
examples.en: Snakes molt several times as they grow.
I photographed an insect's molting process.
If you want change, start by breaking away from the mold.

examples.ko: 과거 이미지의 탈피를 위해 로고를 바꿨어요.
examples.en: We changed the logo to break away from the old image.
Right after molting, a crab's shell is soft.

explain: 곤충, 뱀, 게가 껍질을 벗을 때도 쓰고, 낡은 생각이나 방식에서 벗어난다는 비유로도 써요. 비유에서는 '낡은 관행에서의 탈피'처럼 조사 '에서'와 함께 써요. 동사는 '탈피하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when insects, snakes or crabs shed their skin, and also figuratively for breaking away from old ideas or ways. In the figurative use it goes with '에서', as in '낡은 관행에서의 탈피'. The verb is '탈피하다'.

examples.en: Snakes molt several times as they grow.
I want to break away from old habits.

examples.ko: 매미는 나무 위에서 탈피한 뒤에 날아요.
examples.en: Cicadas fly after molting on a tree.

examples.ko: 옛날 방식에서 탈피해서 새 앱을 만들었어요.
examples.en: We broke away from the old way and made a new app.
A crab grows bigger each time it molts.
Without breaking away from the mold, there is no progress.

explain: 곤충, 뱀 같은 동물이 껍질을 벗을 때도 쓰고, 사람이 낡은 생각이나 방식을 버릴 때도 써요. 사람 이야기에서는 '~에서 탈피하다'로 쓰고 '벗어나다'보다 조금 딱딱해요.
explain_en: It is used when animals such as insects and snakes shed their skin, and also when a person gives up old thinking or ways. For people it is '~에서 탈피하다', which sounds a bit stiffer than '벗어나다'.

examples.ko: 옛이야기에 나오는 현자는 항상 조용히 조언해요.
examples.en: The sage in old tales always gives advice quietly.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 현자를 찾아가 길을 물었어요.
examples.en: The villagers went to the sage and asked for guidance.
A single word from the sage changed everyone's mind.

examples.ko: 이 영화에는 산속에 사는 현자가 나와요.
examples.en: A sage who lives in the mountains appears in this movie.
I have a friend who speaks calmly like a sage.

examples.ko: 이 책에서 동양의 여러 현자를 소개했어요.
examples.en: This book introduces several sages of the East.

explain: '똑똑한 사람'은 머리가 좋은 사람이고, '현자'는 경험과 지혜가 깊어 조언을 줄 수 있는 사람이에요. 옛이야기, 소설, 영화에서 주로 보고, 일상에서 친구를 현자라고 부르면 칭찬이나 농담이에요.
explain_en: A '똑똑한 사람' is simply smart, while a '현자' has deep experience and wisdom and can give advice. You mostly meet the word in old tales, novels and films; calling a friend a '현자' in daily life is a compliment or a joke.

examples.en: Firecrackers contain gunpowder.
I was startled because I smelled gunpowder.
They say gunpowder was first invented in China.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 화약을 쓸 때는 허가가 필요해요.
examples.en: Using gunpowder at a construction site requires permission.
After the fireworks ended, the gunpowder smoke hung thick.
In the old days, guns were fired with gunpowder.

explain: '화약'은 폭죽, 총, 대포에 들어가는 재료이고, '폭탄'은 완성된 무기예요. 보통 '화약 냄새', '화약 연기'처럼 써요. 비유로 곧 터질 듯 위험한 곳을 '화약고'라고 해요.
explain_en: '화약' is the material that goes into firecrackers, guns and cannons, while '폭탄' is the finished weapon. Typical uses are '화약 냄새' and '화약 연기'. Figuratively, a place about to blow up is called a '화약고'.

examples.en: That country was once very strong and prosperous.

examples.ko: 강성한 나라가 되려면 경제가 튼튼해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a strong and prosperous nation, the economy must be sound.

examples.ko: 고구려는 광개토대왕 때 가장 강성했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say Goguryeo was at its strongest under King Gwanggaeto.
When its power grew strong, neighboring countries became wary.
Even the once-mighty kingdom eventually fell.
I dream of a strong and peaceful country.

explain: '강하다'는 사람, 물건, 감정 어디에나 쓰지만 '강성하다'는 나라, 왕조, 세력이 힘이 세고 번성할 때만 써요. 역사 이야기에서 '강성한 나라', '강성해지다'로 자주 나와요. 반대는 '쇠퇴하다'예요.
explain_en: '강하다' can describe people, things or feelings, but '강성하다' is only for a nation, dynasty or power that is strong and thriving. In history stories you see '강성한 나라' and '강성해지다'. The opposite is '쇠퇴하다'.
